extracted_from.note: Page loaded via WebFetch. CSS tokens not capturable — styles in external Next.js CSS Modules. Structural data (headings, CTAs, sections, trust signals) fully captured.

extracted_from.source: 官网分析 (Playwright browser + HTML extraction)
extracted_from.note: Browser evaluate captured computed CSS: body font, h1/h2 sizes/weights/colors, card shadows/radius, section backgrounds, button styles. HTML extraction yielded 4 hex colors and Tailwind class tokens (teal-*, ocean-*).
Incapsula/Imperva bot protection. Curl returns challenge page (212 bytes). StealthyFetcher + DynamicFetcher both fail with timeout. Design tokens supplemented from known brand identity.
Same Incapsula protection as Regus (both IWG-owned). Curl returns challenge page (212 bytes). Design tokens supplemented from known brand identity and IWG family design language.

palette.primary_role: 主色 — dark teal/green. Used for primary buttons (filled on hover), nav CTAs, brand identity. Conveys premium, calm, established trust.
palette.accent_role: 强调色 — warm gold/amber. Used for star ratings, checkmark icons (SVG), promotional badges. Adds warmth against cool teal/navy palette.
palette.surface_role: 背景色层次 — white (cards/hero text), light gray-blue #F5F7F9 (content sections), warm gray #F7F7F7 (alternating sections), near-black #181A1D (dark value-prop sections, footer areas). Coworking sites use a dark section for contrast — usually the testimonial or 'why us' section.
palette.neutral_role: 文字颜色 — near-black #181A1D for body text (never pure #000), medium gray #65666A for secondary/link text. On dark sections: white #FFFFFF.
palette.border_role: 边框颜色 — light gray for card borders, form inputs. Outlined buttons use the teal primary as border color.

h1.note: Hero H1: 48px on Industrious, WeWork similar range. Often white on dark overlay/image background.

h2.note: Section H2: 18px on Industrious (unusually small — used as subhead). Typical coworking H2 is 28-36px.

body.note: 16px on Inter is the coworking standard.

section_padding.note: Standard section: 80px top/bottom, 32-40px horizontal on desktop.

content_max_width.note: Most coworking sites use max-width 1200-1280px containers. Industrious uses full-bleed sections with internal padding.

card_padding.note: Solution/plan cards typically 24-32px padding. Feature cards lean toward 24px.

border_radius.cards: 3px (subtle — Industrious measured value. Other sites may use 8-12px for a softer feel)
border_radius.note: Pill buttons (border-radius: 9999px) are the dominant CTA pattern in coworking. Cards use subtle 3-12px radius. Location search inputs typically 8px.

elevation.shadows: Soft, diffuse shadows with very low opacity. Coworking avoids harsh shadows — the aesthetic is airy, open, light-filled.
typical_values: rgba(0,0,0,0.05) 0px 16px 40px 4px (Industrious card — large blur, minimal opacity)

typical_order: header (sticky nav, transparent on hero, solid on scroll. Logo left, links center-right, CTA button far right)
promo_banner (optional — thin strip above nav with discount/offer. WeWork uses this prominently)
hero (full-width interior photo with dark overlay + white H1 + H2 subhead + embedded city/location search input + 2-4 product selector cards)
client_logo_bar (grayscale/monochrome enterprise logos — 5-8 brands — Pfizer, Microsoft, Salesforce, Amazon, Samsung, Hyatt, etc.)
solutions_grid (3-4 cards: Private Office, Coworking, Meeting Rooms, Enterprise. Icon + H3 + description + 'Learn more' CTA)
value_propositions (2-3 alternating image+text rows — 'Why choose us' narrative with large interior photos)
amenities_section (icon grid — 24/7 access, WiFi, meeting rooms, printing, events, coffee, etc.)
testimonials (carousel or grid of 3-5 member quotes with 5-star ratings, headshots, company names)
news_or_blog (3-4 article cards with thumbnails, category tags, 'Read more')
newsletter_signup (simple email capture, often on brand-color background)
footer (5+ columns: Company, Solutions, Locations, Partners, Support/Contact + social icons + legal + language selector)
hero_variants: Location-search hero (WeWork, Regus): H1 + city dropdown/autocomplete + product selector cards. The hero IS a conversion tool — not just a headline.
Statement hero (Industrious): Bold H1 with italic emphasis + subhead + CTA button + solution cards. More brand-forward, less search-centric.
card_variants: Solution/product cards: Icon + H3 + description + feature checklist (checkmark icons) + 'Learn more' CTA. Used in hero area and solutions grid.
Location cards (if present): Large photo + city name + address + 'View location' CTA.
Testimonial cards: Quote text + 5 gold stars + name + company. Often linked to Google Maps reviews for authenticity.
Article/blog cards: Thumbnail image + category pill/badge + H3 title + excerpt + 'Read more' link.
Plan/membership cards (if pricing page): Plan name + price + feature list + primary CTA. Often 3-column layout with middle column highlighted.

tone_profile.headline_style: Confident, definitive, benefit-forward. Uses italic emphasis on key differentiator words ('The *best* workplace and member experience, period.' — Industrious). WeWork: 'Discover a smarter way to work.' Short, declarative, never passive. Avoids jargon — speaks to business outcomes not real estate terms.
tone_profile.cta_style: Imperative verbs, action-first, benefit-adjacent. Primary: 'Join Now', 'Get Started', 'Book a Tour', 'Find Your Space'. Secondary: 'Learn More', 'Explore', 'View Locations'. Tertiary: 'Read More', 'Read Case Study'. All primary CTAs are 2-3 words max. Never 'Submit' or 'Click here'. The CTA hierarchy is: Book/Join > Explore/Learn > Read/View.
trust_signals: Enterprise client logos (Microsoft, Pfizer, Salesforce, Amazon, Samsung, Visa — grayscale treatment)
Location count ('600+ locations', '250+ locations in 85+ cities')
Star ratings (5-star Google Maps reviews with real names and photos)
Press logos (WSJ, CNBC, Commercial Observer — 'IN THE NEWS' section)
Case studies with named company + real quote + headshot
anti_patterns: DON'T use 'cheap', 'affordable', 'budget' — coworking sells value and experience, not price
DON'T use 'office space' as primary language — say 'workplace', 'workspace', 'space'
DON'T use passive CTAs like 'Submit', 'Click here', 'Find out more'
DON'T use pure black (#000) — use near-black (#181A1D, #1a1a1a)
DON'T use hard shadows — coworking aesthetic is airy and light
DON'T hide pricing completely — even if enterprise-focused, have a 'starting at' somewhere

color_mood: Warm + Professional (Industrious): Teal primary + gold accents + warm grays. Feels established, premium, human-centered. Best for targeting corporate decision-makers who want quality signals.
Bold + Tech-forward (WeWork): Black/white primary + vibrant cyan accent. Minimalist, modern, urban. Best for targeting startups, freelancers, tech companies.
typography_mood: Geometric sans (Inter/SF Pro): Clean, modern, professional. Used by Industrious. Best for enterprise/trust-focused positioning.
Grotesk/neo-grotesk (Apercu/Galano-style): Slightly more personality, wider proportions. Historically WeWork. Best for community/culture-focused positioning.
Mixed serif headings + sans body: Could differentiate a boutique coworking brand. Untapped in major players.
layout_density: Full-bleed + generous whitespace (Industrious): Sections fill viewport width, internal content has breathing room. Feels premium and unhurried.
Contained + card-dense (WeWork/Regus): Max-width containers, tightly packed cards, information-rich. Feels comprehensive and utilitarian.

location_search.description: The defining UX pattern of coworking sites. A city/address autocomplete input embedded directly in the hero section — often the most prominent interactive element after the headline.
location_search.typical_implementation: Text input with dropdown autocomplete listing 50-200+ cities. Commonly paired with a 'Find locations' or 'Search' submit button. The input often has a map-pin or search icon prefix.
location_search.design: Large input (height 48-56px), border-radius 8px, white background, subtle border, prominent placeholder text like 'Find a workplace near you' or 'Search by city, address, or ZIP'.

amenity_icons.description: Grid of 4-8 icons representing key amenities. Almost always monochrome line icons (not filled).

membership_cards.description: When present, membership/plan cards follow a 3-column pattern: Coworking (hot desk), Dedicated Desk, Private Office. Each card has: plan name, per-month price, feature checklist, and a 'Get started' or 'Book a tour' CTA. The middle or rightmost column is often visually highlighted (filled background vs outlined).

interior_photography.description: Coworking sites are photography-heavy. Hero images are large, bright interior shots showing natural light, people working (candid, not staged), plants, modern furniture. Images are warm-toned with medium contrast. Typical treatments: slight warmth added, no heavy filters, natural saturation.
interior_photography.sizes: Hero images typically 1600-2000px wide, 900-1100px tall. Content images 600-900px wide. All delivered as WebP with quality=80-100.
